subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which part of #35203, if any, should OpenClaw accept into core first: a narrow capability/budget seam, a plugin/ClawHub implementation path, or no core work for now?
rationale: The RFC changes state storage, memory visibility, config, delegation authority, and budget enforcement, so automation cannot choose the product/security boundary safely.

options.title: Split a Narrow Core Seam
options.body: Keep the RFC open but only authorize a first slice that defines capability/usage/budget contracts and security rules before any shared memory or blackboard runtime lands.

options.title: Route Full Orchestration to Plugins
options.body: Treat blackboard, learned profiles, and orchestration policy as ClawHub/plugin work unless a concrete missing core API is identified.

options.title: Close as Out of Scope
options.body: Close the RFC if maintainers decide the full multi-agent collaboration stack conflicts with the current lean-core roadmap.

recommendation.title: Split a Narrow Core Seam
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC open but only authorize a first slice that defines capability/usage/budget contracts and security rules before any shared memory or blackboard runtime lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the relevant agent/config surfaces and has already provided scoping feedback on adjacent multi-agent RFCs.
